newsitem.title: MEXICO: Northern Mexico businesses say slump continues.
newsitem.headline: Northern Mexico businesses say slump continues.

text.p: Business activity in the northern Mexican industrial city of Monterrey has yet to recover from the country's economic crisis and has little chance of recovering in 1997, a business leader told reporters Thursday.

"There can scarcely be growth as conditions are not conducive to boosting activity. We need savings to recover, and that will only happen when the government realizes that businesses and individuals need tax breaks to do so," said Jose Garza Benavides, director of the Monterrey National Chamber of Commerce (Canaco).
Garza said 1,400 businesses closed their doors in Monterrey in 1995, and another 500 had done so thus far in 1996, out of a total of 19,000 Canaco members in 1994.
Garza added that although employment in the region had recovered from 1995 levels, it was still 45 percent below 1994 figures.

"Things are slightly better than in 1995, I think macroeconomic figures show that, but that's no reason to hang out the flags ... we will still close down this year, just as we did last year," he said.
